craft_claim: The essay form since Montaigne treats the self as the material of a trial of thought — provisional judgment, self-questioning, and visible revision are its load-bearing devices — which is how the voice can be personal and outward-directed at once without becoming abstract.

supporting_evidence.location: Essais I.26 (De l'institution des enfants), III.13 (De l'expérience), and the author's address to the reader
supporting_evidence.note: Montaigne makes himself the matter of the book, tests general questions against his own habits and body, marks revisions across the 1580/1588/1595 edition layers, and holds his inquiry under a questioning motto; essays proceed by example-from-life, not argument-from-principle.

Lopate frames the anthology as putting forward and interpreting the personal-essay tradition from the classical era to the present; characterizes the essayist as a reliable narrator who has done introspective homework; describes the form as flexible and digressive, circling its subject from all angles; and presents the personal essay as basic research on the self — a mode of inquiry allied with but distinct from philosophy and science.

supporting_evidence.location: 'The Essay as Form', Notes to Literature vol. 1, pp. 29-47
supporting_evidence.note: Adorno defends the essay's method: it does not apply a pre-given method to its object but lets the object come into focus through provisional, non-systematic thought — form as exploration rather than demonstration.

counterevidence.note: Adorno also records the standing charge (condemnation of the essay in German letters) that the form is intellectually irresponsible; the essay's legitimacy is argued, not granted, so the card cannot treat reflective provisionality as self-evidently virtuous.

Lopate names intimacy as the personal essay's hallmark and its reader-relationship as a kind of dialogue or friendship — the tradition's own leading theorist pulls the form toward the tone-intimate side, so this taxonomy's reflective/intimate split (inward thinking vs addressed disclosure) is a deliberate narrowing, not a fact about the tradition.

scope: Nonfiction essay (personal and literary); extends to essayistic reflective passages in fiction, poetry, and copy that borrow the trial-of-thought method.
exceptions: Aphoristic traditions (Bacon, La Rochefoucauld) are essay-adjacent but compressed, general, and outward — philosophical register, not reflective.
The confessional essay (tone-intimate) discloses for closeness; the reflective essay thinks aloud whether or not the reader is addressed.
